Maatteessüf, hoca efendimiz, bu dersi talebelerin bihakkın ve mükemmelen istatistik temeline sahip oldukları faraziyesiyle icra etmekte olup, talebenin “Bu muallim efendi neşr-i ilime dair acaba ne buyurmaktadır ki?” sualini sıkça sormasına sebebiyet vermektedir.

Bununla birlikte, maatteessüf, memleketimizde birçok öğretim üyesinin düştüğü bir hataya kendisi de dûçâr olmuştur; zira akademisyen kimliğini eğitimci kimliğinin önüne koyarak, talebelerinin hakikat-i ders ve ilme vâkıf olmalarını müşkil hale getirmektedir.

İmdi, bu ahvâl, hocamızın ders-i şerifindeki netice-i umumiyenin ekseriyetle 1.20 ila 1.80 gibi noksan bir mertebede tebellür etmesinin en mühim esbab-ı mucibesindendir. Halbuki, kendü, ekonometri ilmine bihakkın vâkıf, mezâyâ-i ilmiye ve kemalât-ı zihniyede mümtaz bir zattır. Lakin, maalesef ki bu meziyetler, bir muallim-i muvaffak olmasına yetmemektedir.

Netice-i kelâm, bu mülahazât ve tenkidatın, zat-ı alisinin ulûm-u ekonometriyeyi daha ziyade muvaffakiyetle neşr ve talim etmesine vesile olmasını temenni eyler, derin hürmet ve tazim ile selam ederim. Saygılarımla.

Taner Hoca has been criticized by some for “not knowing enough mathematics,” but I believe this view is both unfair and reductive. Economics is not a branch of pure mathematics, it’s a social science that requires intuition, reasoning, and the ability to connect abstract models to real-world dynamics. Taner Hoca demonstrates a strong and thoughtful command of economic theory. His strength lies not in mathematical formalism, but in his ability to think critically, ask meaningful questions, and convey why a concept matters beyond the equations. His teaching reminds us that economics is, at its core, about understanding human behavior and societal outcomes.

I had previously taken ECON301 with him as an undergraduate. Looking back, I now realize how much I had missed out on. At the time, I wasn’t mature enough to appreciate the richness of his knowledge. This semester gave me the chance to truly learn from him, and I’m grateful for that.

That said, the course would benefit from a more structured design. It’s not a new course, yet at times the flow felt unplanned, and there were moments where it seemed even Taner Hoca wasn’t fully sure what direction to take. This affected my motivation at times. With clearer organization, the course could be even more effective.

Still, Taner Hoca consistently tried to draw us in, through examples, stories, and human reflections. Even in a topic I personally found quite dry, he worked hard to make us care. And beyond economics, he shared wisdom that will stay with me. One thing he said truly moved me: “You will most probably lose because you are a good person, but please, be a good person. Don’t break others so easily.”
That sentence alone made this course unforgettable.  I am deeply grateful for what I have learned from him, both academically and personally. Thank you hocam :)
